handoff.purpose: Defines utility functions for gh command construction, failure classification, URL extraction; defines STATUS_NO_TRANSCRIPT constant; defines load_for_publish function to reconstruct verdict and turns from stored bus transcript.

symbols.name: _gh_argv
symbols.note: Constructs a list of command-line arguments from a base list and an optional repo string; if repo is provided, appends ['--repo', str(repo)].

symbols.name: _classify_failure
symbols.note: Maps a failed gh invocation (RunResult) to a tuple (status, detail). Checks stderr and stdout for specific error patterns, ordered: gh missing, auth failure, rate limit, PR not found, generic error.

symbols.name: _first_url
symbols.note: Extracts the first URL (http or https) from a string by splitting on whitespace and checking prefixes.

symbols.name: STATUS_NO_TRANSCRIPT
symbols.note: String constant 'no_transcript' used as a status value.

symbols.name: load_for_publish
symbols.note: Reconstructs (verdict, turns) from a stored bus transcript file. Parses transcript records to extract council_id, question, requested vendors (from roster), and answered vendors (from turn records with status 'spoke'). Returns a verdict dict and the full turns list.

claims.text: Auth is tested before not-found because GitHub answers 404 -- not 403 -- for a private repo you are not authenticated to see; classifying that as ``pr_not_found`` would send an operator hunting for a PR that exists and is merely invisible to a logged-out CLI.
claims.why: The code checks auth-related patterns before 'not found'/'404' patterns, consistent with the claim's ordering rationale.

claims.text: ``(verdict, turns)`` reconstructed from a stored bus transcript.
claims.why: The function returns a tuple (verdict, turns) as shown at the end of the chunk (though the return statement is not fully visible, the docstring describes it).

claims.text: The council package stores no ``outcome`` and no ``convergence`` field -- by construction, because it promotes nothing -- so none is invented here, and :func:`render_markdown` prints "(not recorded)" for them.
claims.why: This claim refers to the behaviour of another module (render_markdown) and the council package's data model, neither of which is present in this chunk.

claims.text: Quorum comes from the roster records' ``participants``: a vendor is ANSWERED only if it actually produced a turn, not if it was merely seated.
claims.why: The code initializes answered as empty list and only appends actors from turn records where status == 'spoke', as documented. Requested vendors come from roster records.

claims.text: This was written the obvious way first -- any turn with a vendor on it -- and it was WRONG, caught against a real transcript (runs/council/council-20260728T121214Z-a5241ac5.jsonl): that council has four turn records but two of them are placeholders, google `not_authenticated` and openai `not_on_path`, and the bus itself records `responded: 2, degraded: true`. The naive version rendered "Quorum: 4 of 4 (full roster)" over a council where half the vendors never ran -- silently upgrading a degraded council to a full one, which is the single most misleading thing this renderer could say, since independence is the only thing a multi-vendor council buys.
claims.why: This claim references a specific historical transcript file and a previous bug; neither the file nor the bug fix is verifiable in this chunk.

observations.what: _classify_failure checks for auth patterns before 'not found' patterns, consistent with its docstring claim about GitHub returning 404 for unauthorized access to private repos.
load_for_publish correctly distinguishes requested from answered vendors: requested from roster records, answered only from turn records with status 'spoke'.

The function load_for_publish imports bus from the parent package and calls bus.load_transcript; the import statement is present, but the actual implementation of bus.load_transcript is not in this chunk.
The verdict dict includes 'bus_path' with the store path converted to forward slashes; the rest of the verdict construction is not fully visible in this chunk.
The function uses helper functions _text, _field, _as_list which are defined elsewhere in the same file; their exact behaviour is not verified here.
